answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake and earn a portable reputation record before it can transact. Like a jetty that narrows a harbor entrance to one guarded channel, the stake makes every new identity expensive: an attacker splitting funds across a thousand fake agents dilutes each one's stake below the trust threshold. Each verified job mints a jade-grade attestation that accumulates into a relic of proven work no sockpuppet can fake, and misbehavior slashes the stake, so forgery costs money while honesty compounds.
